composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# First step: read the optional 'Idempotency-Key' header. When the key was already seen, replay
# the originally created owner with 200 (thrown as an escalation) rather than creating a duplicate.
# Ungoverned: a replay short-circuits here before any write, so no transaction is opened.
checkIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotencyKey
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectFutureRegistrationDate

# Reject a supplied registrationDate later than the server date (400) before it is
# defaulted or rolled to a business day, so the check sees the raw supplied value.
rejectFutureRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectFutureRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: defaultRegistrationDate

defaultRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.DefaultOwnerRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalize

normalize:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerTelephone
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeEmail

normalizeEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerEmail
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectDisposableEmailDomain

rejectDisposableEmailDomain:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectDisposableEmailDomain
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeAddress

normalizeAddress:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerAddress
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectInvalidPostcode

# Validate the postcode (when present) against the region derived from the city.
rejectInvalidPostcode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectInvalidPostcode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# Derive the deterministic householdId (SHA-256 over normalizedLastName+'|'+postcode)
# first, so the next step can detect owners that fall into an existing household.
assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectDuplicateIdentity

# Single duplicate check: reject only an exact identityKey match (SHA-256 over
# normalizedTelephone|lowerEmail|soundex(lastName)). The computed householdId no longer
# feeds duplicate detection, so same-household owners with different telephones are allowed.
rejectDuplicateIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectDuplicateOwnerIdentity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectCityCapacity

rejectCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectOwnerCityAtCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectDailyLimit

rejectDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectOwnerDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignPossibleDuplicate

# Not a hard duplicate (already past rejectDuplicateIdentity), but flag when it shares an
# existing owner's lastName and postcode with a different telephone: possibleDuplicate.
# A declared household member (sharesHousehold) is exempt: it is not a suspected duplicate.
assignPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHouseholdSize

assignHouseholdSize:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerHouseholdSize
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: capMembershipLevel

# Cap the derived membershipLevel at one above the current maximum among existing
# household members (no cap when the owner has no existing household member).
capMembershipLevel:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CapOwnerMembershipLevel
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignNamesakeCount

assignNamesakeCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignBulkSignupWarning

assignBulkSignupWarning:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerBulkSignupWarning
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: recordIdempotency

# Record the created owner against the request's Idempotency-Key (no-op when absent), so a
# later create with the same key replays this owner instead of creating a duplicate.
recordIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RecordIdempotencyKey
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

The full suite is green: **255 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, BUILD SUCCESS**.

## Summary

I implemented the structured audit event in the one place the create pipeline already audits owners: `AuditOwnerCreated` (the `audit` step in `owners.POST.yml`, which runs after `SaveOwner` so the persisted id is available).

Changes to `src/main/java/.../rest/function/owner/AuditOwnerCreated.java`:

- **Kept** the existing human-readable audit line unchanged.
- **Added** an immutable structured JSON event emitted on the same `AUDIT` logger:
  `{"seq":…,"ownerId":…,"customerCode":…,"membershipLevel":…,"event":"OWNER_CREATED"}`
- **`seq`** is a process-wide `AtomicLong` (`SEQUENCE.incrementAndGet()`), giving a monotonically increasing integer across all creates.
- **Primary-identifier evolution**: the `customerCode` value is read through a single `primaryIdentifier(Owner)` helper. Today it returns `owner.getCustomerCode()`; when the customerCode is later unified into a memberId, that one method is the sole switch point and the event value tracks whatever the primary identifier becomes (the JSON key stays `customerCode` as the spec fixes it).
- JSON is built with a small `quote(...)` escaper so the event is well-formed even if a value ever contains special characters.

The new `AcceptanceTest.coreEventCarriesIdAndIdentifier` passes — the AUDIT capture confirms a line like `{"seq":1,"ownerId":11,"customerCode":"NSW-16E6609E","membershipLevel":1,"event":"OWNER_CREATED"}` — and no existing tests regressed.
